jobs.title: Director, Data Engineering (Permanent/full-time)
jobs.description:
CoreFactor is searching for a Director, Data Engineering on a permanent/full-time basis for a client in the GTA.

This position is hybrid and will require the successful incumbent to go into the office two (2) days per week.

As Director, Data Engineering within our clients Global Technology & Data Team, you'll play a pivotal role in shaping and executing the organization's enterprise data engineering strategy across a complex multi-cloud environment. Partnering closely with data leadership, enterprise architecture, and technology stakeholders, you will lead the design, delivery, and operation of scalable data platforms and services that enable business transformation, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision making across North America and globally.

This is an opportunity to leverage your expertise to help drive the organizations' next-generation data ecosystem, modernize our enterprise data platforms, and position the organization for continued innovation and growth.

The Role:

Lead enterprise data engineering strategy: Direct and scale a high-performing team of managers and data engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and technical excellence.
Drive modern data platform delivery: Oversee the design, development, and implementation of enterprise-scale data platforms, including microservices architectures, data mesh and data fabric capabilities, AI/ML pipelines, Agentic AI and GenAI workflows, document extraction services, and business intelligence solutions.
Champion technology roadmap and innovation: Partner with Enterprise Architecture, product leaders, vendors, and technology stakeholders to define and execute the long-term data engineering roadmap, ensuring alignment with regional and global business objectives.
Establish operational excellence and DataOps practices: Define and enforce standards for DataOps, SDLC, CI/CD, data governance, security, documentation, code quality, and AI-enabled delivery methodologies to ensure scalable and reliable platform operations.
Ensure platform reliability and service excellence: Oversee the operational health, performance, and support of critical North American and global data products, driving incident management, platform availability, and adherence to enterprise service level agreements (SLAs).

Requirements

Degree and/or diploma in: Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline. Master’s degree preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
8-10 years of progressive experience, preferably in: data engineering, data platform, cloud engineering, enterprise data architecture, or related technology leadership roles, including experience managing managers and technical professionals.
Proven experience in cloud-based data architecture and engineering: Deep expertise designing and scaling enterprise data platforms using Google Cloud Platform services such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage, Dataproc, Cloud Data Fusion, Cloud Run, and Apigee.
Strong proficiency in modern engineering practices and tools: Experience with Kubernetes, particularly GKE, microservices architecture, enterprise APIs, serverless computing, infrastructure-as-code using Terraform, Azure DevOps, and CI/CD frameworks.
Strategic understanding of BI, analytics, and artificial intelligence: Knowledge of semantic data models, Looker, Power BI, machine learning pipelines, and AI-driven solutions that accelerate engineering delivery and operational excellence.
Exceptional leadership and communication skills: Ability to influence senior leaders, align cross-functional teams, translate technical strategy into measurable business outcomes, and build a strong culture of accountability and collaboration.
Commercial real estate industry experience: Considered an asset.

jobs.title: Chief Architect & Design Authority
jobs.description:
Req ID:
397927

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a Chief Architect & Design Authority to join our team in Remote, British Columbia (CA-BC), Canada (CA).

Purpose of the role

Global Platforms is moving to a product-led platform organization in which AI agents run more and more of the service-management work, under clear governance. This Chief Architect & Design Authority position will be the single design authority for that platform. This role sets the architecture, standards and certification that every team builds and deploys against, independently of any one build or delivery team. The role reports to the Head of Core Engineering because its standards apply equally across all four pillars. Keeping design authority separate from build and run accountability means standards stay consistent and reusable, and are never relaxed to meet one team's delivery pressure.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture and standards
Own the Global Platforms reference architecture: One NTT Platform foundation, One Experience Platform, Composable modules, cloud tools and client tools.
Define and maintain the Agentic Service Management reference model: ITIL 4 practices as the process map, IT4IT as the reference architecture, and a standard decomposition from process to vendor adapter.
Set vendor-neutral interface standards (including MCP-based tool interfaces) and adapter conformance tests.
Define the action envelope standard.
Design authority and certification
Chair the platform design authority.
Certify agents, automations and action envelopes before production or delivery.
Own the agent and automation registry standard.
Agentic platform architecture
Lead the architecture of the NTT-owned control plane.
Provide technical oversight of the Incident process PoC and Phase 2 design.
Keep portable process specifications and envelope catalogue outside any single vendor.
Technology strategy and vendor architecture
Advise on build, buy or integrate decisions.
Shape partner architecture relationships with ServiceNow, Microsoft, LogicMonitor, Cisco and hyperscalers.
Own cloud tools architecture.
Provide tooling rationalization input.
Engineering standards
Set architectural guardrails for CI/CD, testing, IaC, SRE and golden paths.
Ensure self-service capabilities support engineering and composable modules.
Client and security engagement
Represent architecture to client boards.
Work with the CISO office on security architecture.
Innovation and people
Assess innovation funnel opportunities.
Lead and develop the architecture team and community of practice.

Key relationships

Global Head of Platform Technology & Innovation.
Head of Engineering, Global Platform: line manager.
Pillar leads: peers and consumers of standards.
Release & Service Introduction lead: joint owner of certification.
C&S delivery, sales and solution architecture leadership.
CISO office.
Partners: ServiceNow, Microsoft, LogicMonitor, Cisco, hyperscalers.

Decision rights

Decides: reference architecture, standards, approvals and certification outcomes.
Recommends: build/buy/integrate, vendor choices, investment priorities.
Escalates: disputed design authority decisions and exceptions.

Success measures (first 12 months)

Reference architecture and Agentic Service Management standards adopted.
Design authority and certification operating with production agents registered and certified.
Phase 1 Agentic Operation delivered and Phase 2 approved.
Interface standards and conformance tests in use.
Architecture input into license rationalization and FY27 planning.
Architecture community established.

Experience And Capabilities

Senior enterprise or platform architect with 15+ years experience.
Experience setting and enforcing architecture standards.
Knowledge of ITIL 4 and IT4IT or equivalent.
Experience with automation, AIOps, observability and agentic/GenAI systems.
Knowledge of ServiceNow and hyperscaler AI platforms.
Integration architecture experience.
Able to engage with CIOs, architecture and security boards.
Desirable: ITIL4, IT4IT, TOGAF or equivalent.

jobs.title: AVP, Technology Lead - Digital
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Role Summary

The AVP Technology Lead – Digital is a strategic technology leader responsible for enabling, scaling, and modernizing Sun Life Canada’s shared digital platforms that support secure, connected, and frictionless Client and advisor experiences. This role provides technology leadership across core digital assets including Secure Web, Public Web, & Secure Mobile, and related enablement platforms such as client identity and access management, and an internal design system.

The role combines strategic leadership, technical oversight, people leadership, delivery execution, operational accountability, and vendor/financial management to drive technology excellence and measurable business value. The AVP partners closely with Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, Engineering, and Business leaders to ensure digital assets are resilient, scalable, secure, reusable, and aligned to enterprise priorities.

This role operates in a complex, high-visibility environment where digital platform reliability, modernization, and cross-business enablement are critical to Client outcomes. The leader must be able to bring clarity to a broad mandate, make decisions in ambiguity, and build a high-performing technology organization that balances speed, stability, security, and long-term platform health.

What will you do?

Technology Strategy, Platform Enablement & Engineering
Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.
Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.
Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.
Promote technology stack standards, modern engineering practices, automation, and architectural discipline, balancing build vs. buy vs. partner decisions in a complex technology ecosystem.
Ensure design and engineering decisions account for reusability, scalability, security, maintainability, accessibility, and technical debt reduction.
Create the conditions for exceptional digital experiences by enabling business and product teams with reliable, scalable, secure, and reusable platforms.
Platform Delivery & Execution
Accountable for end-to-end delivery of digital platform capabilities, including oversight of internal delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and total cost of ownership.
Drive delivery excellence by improving velocity, quality, reliability, predictability, and agile maturity across multiple squads.
Track delivery metrics, identify bottlenecks, and implement targeted productivity and delivery maturity improvements.
Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.
Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture, engineering, operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.
Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.
People Leadership & Capability Development
Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.
Design and optimize team structures to support clear ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.
Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.
Build internal capability in digital engineering, enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.
Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.
Financial & Vendor Management
Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.
Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.
Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.
Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.
Operational Excellence, Risk & Security
Ensure stability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.
Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.
Partner with Application Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.
Proactively manage operational risk, application health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.
Communicate digital strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.
Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.
Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.

Accountabilities

Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.
Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.
Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.
Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.
Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.
Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.
Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.

What you need to succeed?

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.
10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.
Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.
Proven ability to lead technology teams through transformation, platform ownership, and operating model evolution.
Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.
Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.
Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide

Mindset & Behaviours

Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.
Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.
Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.
Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term application health.
Collaborative leader who builds trust, drives momentum, and creates clarity across complex stakeholder groups.
Critical thinker who challenges the status quo constructively and drives continuous improvement.
Strong coaching orientation with a commitment to developing leaders, teams, and internal capability.

What’s in it for you?

A competitive salary and bonus program, based on market scale
A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.
Time off that allows you to focus on the moments that matter most. 20 vacation days per year.
Our Share Ownership Program gives you the opportunity to invest in Sun Life while benefiting from employer matching contributions.
We are proud to be included in Great Place to Work's 2026 list of Canada's Best Workplaces.
A warm, supportive, and inclusive culture.

In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

Location: Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

An established Canadian professional services organization is seeking an experienced Director of Microsoft Business Applications to join its leadership team in Vancouver.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for someone with a strong background across Microsoft Dynamics 365, particularly Customer Engagement (CE), Power Platform and enterprise application strategy.

You will take ownership of the organization's Microsoft business applications portfolio, providing strategic, architectural and operational leadership across Dynamics 365, Power Platform, custom applications and integrations.

Working closely with senior stakeholders, you'll lead teams across application development, applications support and the Dynamics Centre of Excellence, driving technology strategy, overseeing major implementations and ensuring solutions are scalable, secure and aligned with wider business objectives.

What's on Offer?

Salary of up to $220,000 CAD.
Hybrid working arrangements.
Opportunity to become a company Shareholder.
Competitive pension and comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits.
Generous paid vacation, additional holiday closure and paid sick leave.
Fitness allowance, parental leave top-up and employee assistance programmes.
Ongoing professional development and career progression opportunities.

What You'll Do

Microsoft Business Applications Strategy

Develop and lead the strategic roadmap across Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, ensuring alignment with wider business objectives.
Oversee the Dynamics Centre of Excellence, driving platform adoption, governance and continuous improvement.
Lead the architecture, implementation and enhancement of Dynamics 365 solutions, with particular emphasis on Customer Engagement (CE), Dataverse, Model-Driven Apps, Power Apps and Power Automate.

Enterprise Applications & Delivery

Establish application development strategies, technical standards and governance across custom applications, integrations and automation.
Provide leadership across major Dynamics 365 implementations, upgrades, integrations and wider enterprise application transformations.
Oversee the full application lifecycle, from requirements gathering and solution design through to delivery, testing and ongoing support.
Ensure solutions are secure, scalable and aligned with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity and data governance standards.
Drive best practices around Azure integrations, CI/CD, source control, environment management and secure development.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

Lead and develop multidisciplinary teams across application development, applications support and the Dynamics Centre of Excellence.
Manage enterprise application budgets, licensing, vendor relationships, contracts and technology investments.
Partner with senior stakeholders across Finance, HR, Operations and Project Delivery to identify opportunities for technology-driven business improvements.
Champion platform adoption, collaboration and continuous improvement across the organization.

Does This Sound Like You?

13+ experience across enterprise technology, business systems or enterprise applications, including at least five years in senior management or director-level leadership.
Significant experience leading Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform environments, ideally with a strong background in
Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (CE).
Strong understanding of D365 CE architecture, Dataverse, Model-Driven Apps, Power Apps and Power Automate.
Experience leading large-scale Dynamics 365 implementations, integrations and enterprise application transformations.
Technical understanding of Azure integrations, Microsoft 365, Power BI and the wider Microsoft ecosystem.
Experience leading application development, support and Centre of Excellence teams.
Strong understanding of enterprise architecture, application governance, integration strategies and secure development practices.
Experience managing budgets, licensing, vendors, system integrators and multidisciplinary teams.
Understanding of professional services processes, including project accounting, resource management, time and expense, billing and customer engagement.
Previous experience within engineering, consulting or professional services environments would be beneficial.

About the Organization

An established Canadian professional services organization, the business delivers a diverse range of projects that help shape communities across Canada.

With a strong focus on sustainability, innovation and long-term growth, the organization prides itself on providing a collaborative environment where employees are supported through professional development, career progression and opportunities to make a meaningful impact.

jobs.title: Director of Business Technology
jobs.description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Keep Things Running

Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

Own the Platforms

Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

Govern and Teach

Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

Team and Partners

Lead two on-site IT staff.
Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

Strong candidates will bring:

Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:
An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare chance to shape how an established Canadian manufacturer builds and runs its technology at a moment when AI is changing who can create software.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

WHAT WE OFFER

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

TO APPLY

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.

President: lead a specialty piling contractor to $50M

VersaPile Inc. | Alberta or Manitoba | Reports to the Founder and Executive Chair

If you have run piling operations, you already know what most construction executives never learn: schedules move, ground conditions surprise you, receivables slip, and critical equipment fails far from major centres. If that sounds like a normal week, and you are good at it, keep reading. If it sounds exhausting, this is not your job.

The mission

Our founder is moving to Executive Chair, and we are hiring a President to take over day-to-day leadership of the company.
Run VersaPile day to day and help turn a fast-growing, dynamic business into a mature and predictable one.
Build the systems and leaders that make clients treat VersaPile as an extension of their own team.
Lead a 100% Indigenous-owned company that combines Indigenous ways of thinking with strong Western business practice.
Help drive the company toward becoming Canada's leader in high-capacity helical piles for energy and utilities.

Why this seat is rare

You get the whole company.
The leadership team reports to you.
The platform is built.
We have operations in Alberta and Manitoba, about 35 full-time staff, and what is likely the country's most capable high-capacity helical pile fleet.
Blue-chip clients.
They include Enbridge, Suncor, CNRL, Worley, Valard, Forbes Bros., Aecon, Hydro One and Manitoba Hydro.
High-bar project sites.
Our clients demand excellence in safety, quality and execution, and so do we.
You win when we win.
The compensation package will be designed for the successful candidate to win alongside the company.

What you will deliver

In your first 12 months

The leadership team reports to you in practice, not just on the org chart.
The annual plan is met on safety, revenue, margin and cash.
The org chart is restructured into one that supports who we are today and where we are going, and every leadership seat is held by someone you would rehire.
Clients and partners see continuity through the leadership transition and notice the improvements.

Within three years

75% of revenue comes from repeat clients.
More than 66% of the business is in energy and utilities.
At least 25% of the workforce is Indigenous, and at least 25% of vendor spend goes to Indigenous suppliers.
VersaPile is in a strong financial position, with cash reserves and shareholder distributions.

You are our person if

You have 10 or more years in piling and deep foundations, or in closely related trades such as transmission and distribution construction, pipeline, specialty drilling, heavy civil or industrial earthworks.
You have carried full profit-and-loss responsibility for a project-based business of $30M or more.
You have personally negotiated contracts, change orders, payment terms and holdback releases with clients who still want to work with you.
You manage cash as closely as margin.
You have led through a crisis, and you know what to do in the first hour and the first week.
You build leaders, hold them accountable, and turn ideas into plans.
You will report effectively to the founder and Executive Chair, and to our Advisory Board.

Experience working with Indigenous communities and businesses is an asset. Indigenous candidates are encouraged to apply.

This is not for you if

You need a stable schedule and a plan that survives the week.
Your experience is in general contracting, where you control the schedule.
You hand hard client conversations to a lawyer or a project manager.
You manage from the office instead of leading across regions and sites.
You see Indigenous ownership as a line in a proposal rather than something that shapes hiring, purchasing and daily decisions.

Compensation and location

A comprehensive executive compensation package may include a combination of base salary, performance incentives, phantom equity, benefits, RRSP match and a vehicle.
You will live in Alberta or Manitoba and travel regularly between the two regions.

How to apply

Send your resume and a short note, one page at most, answering these three questions:
What is the largest profit and loss you have personally owned, and what happened to revenue and margin while you owned it?
Describe the hardest commercial negotiation you have led with a client. What was at stake, and how did it end?
What is the most challenging or complex change initiative you have led? What did the initiative achieve?

We read every note. Applications without one will not be considered.

Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian commercial lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees, selling across Canada and the United States. We are adding a Director of Business Technology to our leadership team, a senior, hands-on role with ownership of technology across the business.

The role has two halves. The first is the job every growing company needs: keep our technology running, secure and recoverable across roughly 130 computers, Microsoft 365, our server cluster and our network. The second is newer. Our own people, from the three Co-Presidents to staff in Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service, now build software tools with AI assistants. The Director of Business Technology will give that work a professional backbone: version control, permissions, backups and fast recovery.

This is an enabling role as much as a technical one. We want our people to keep building quickly. The person in this position will make sure what they build is safe, recoverable and well looked after, without slowing anyone down.

This is a build role. Liteline’s people are already creating their own tools with AI. We are looking for a leader who can keep the core IT environment solid, put the right platforms and guardrails under home-built software, and teach non-programmers to work safely.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Keep Things Running

Own day-to-day IT across the business: computers, email, servers, networking, security and backups.
Run Microsoft 365, including sign-in, multi-factor authentication (MFA), user access and licensing.
Look after our on-premises server cluster, storage and network infrastructure.
Oversee security monitoring and incident response together with our security monitoring partner.
Maintain tested backups and the ability to restore systems and data quickly.
Lead the help desk and set the service standards the business is held to.

Own the Platforms

Set up and run, hands-on, the platforms our home-built tools live on.
Own Liteline’s company GitHub organization, where code is saved with full history, including structure, permissions, single sign-on (SSO) and branch protection.
Administer hosted databases (Supabase / Postgres), including access control, backups and recovery.
Manage website and application hosting (Netlify), including deployments, domains and environments.
Maintain a clear inventory of the tools in use, who owns each one and where it runs.

Govern and Teach

Decide what AI assistants can access and set sensible guardrails for company data and credentials.
Set light, practical rules that protect the business without getting in the way of the people building.
Decide which home-built tools are business-critical and what level of protection each one needs.
Run and rehearse restores so that recovery is proven, not assumed.
Teach staff who are not programmers to work safely, for example explaining version control to someone in purchasing.
Run training, enablement and “lunch and learn” sessions across the business.

Team and Partners

Lead two on-site IT staff.
Manage our outside partners for managed services, security monitoring and backup.
Own the technology budget, licensing and vendor relationships, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a hands-on technology leader who is equally comfortable running core IT and building platforms that sit under modern, AI-assisted development.

The successful candidate will understand infrastructure, identity and security, and will also understand how software is built, saved, deployed and recovered. Just as importantly, you will be able to explain those ideas in plain language to people who have never written code and help them adopt habits that last.

Strong candidates will bring:

Hands-on experience setting up or administering a GitHub organization, including SSO and branch protection.
Experience running a Microsoft Power Platform Centre of Excellence, citizen-developer or low-code programme.
Hands-on experience running Supabase, Postgres, Netlify, Vercel or similar platforms.
Solid Microsoft 365, identity, MFA, endpoint and security fundamentals.
A track record of training and enabling non-technical staff, such as “lunch and learn” or enablement programmes.
Experience building a function or process from scratch at a growing company.
Clear communication and sound judgment about when rules help and when they get in the way.

There is no single path to this role. You might be:
An IT lead at a 100-to-500-person manufacturer or distributor who personally ran a Power Platform governance programme, a low-code programme or the company’s GitHub organization.
A developer or DevOps engineer who moved into an IT management role at a small or mid-sized company.
A solutions architect or senior consultant at a managed services provider (MSP) serving small and mid-sized businesses, ready to go in-house.
The “first IT hire” at a startup who set up sign-in, devices and GitHub from scratch, then moved to a mid-sized company.
Experience in mid-sized manufacturing, distribution or wholesale is helpful but not required.

REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

This position reports to the VP of Operations.

You will work closely with Liteline’s three Co-Presidents, who are technically capable and build their own tools, and with Finance, Product Development, Engineering and Customer Service. You will be a partner to the people building, not a gatekeeper.

LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. Our leaders build with technology themselves and value this work. The Director of Business Technology will define the platforms, guardrails and habits that let the whole company build with confidence.

VersaPile Inc. | Alberta or Manitoba | Reports to the Founder and Executive Chair

If you have run piling operations, you already know what most construction executives never learn: schedules move, ground conditions surprise you, receivables slip, and critical equipment fails far from major centres. If that sounds like a normal week, and you are good at it, keep reading. If it sounds exhausting, this is not your job.

The mission

Our founder is moving to Executive Chair, and we are hiring a President to take over day-to-day leadership of the company.
Run VersaPile day to day and help turn a fast-growing, dynamic business into a mature and predictable one.
Build the systems and leaders that make clients treat VersaPile as an extension of their own team.
Lead a 100% Indigenous-owned company that combines Indigenous ways of thinking with strong Western business practice.
Help drive the company toward becoming Canada's leader in high-capacity helical piles for energy and utilities.

Why this seat is rare

You get the whole company.
The leadership team reports to you.
The platform is built.
We have operations in Alberta and Manitoba, about 35 full-time staff, and what is likely the country's most capable high-capacity helical pile fleet.
Blue-chip clients.
They include Enbridge, Suncor, CNRL, Worley, Valard, Forbes Bros., Aecon, Hydro One and Manitoba Hydro.
High-bar project sites.
Our clients demand excellence in safety, quality and execution, and so do we.
You win when we win.
The compensation package will be designed for the successful candidate to win alongside the company.

What you will deliver

In your first 12 months

The leadership team reports to you in practice, not just on the org chart.
The annual plan is met on safety, revenue, margin and cash.
The org chart is restructured into one that supports who we are today and where we are going, and every leadership seat is held by someone you would rehire.
Clients and partners see continuity through the leadership transition and notice the improvements.

Within three years

75% of revenue comes from repeat clients.
More than 66% of the business is in energy and utilities.
At least 25% of the workforce is Indigenous, and at least 25% of vendor spend goes to Indigenous suppliers.
VersaPile is in a strong financial position, with cash reserves and shareholder distributions.

You are our person if

You have 10 or more years in piling and deep foundations, or in closely related trades such as transmission and distribution construction, pipeline, specialty drilling, heavy civil or industrial earthworks.
You have carried full profit-and-loss responsibility for a project-based business of $30M or more.
You have personally negotiated contracts, change orders, payment terms and holdback releases with clients who still want to work with you.
You manage cash as closely as margin.
You have led through a crisis, and you know what to do in the first hour and the first week.
You build leaders, hold them accountable, and turn ideas into plans.
You will report effectively to the founder and Executive Chair, and to our Advisory Board.

Experience working with Indigenous communities and businesses is an asset. Indigenous candidates are encouraged to apply.

This is not for you if

You need a stable schedule and a plan that survives the week.
Your experience is in general contracting, where you control the schedule.
You hand hard client conversations to a lawyer or a project manager.
You manage from the office instead of leading across regions and sites.
You see Indigenous ownership as a line in a proposal rather than something that shapes hiring, purchasing and daily decisions.

A comprehensive executive compensation package may include a combination of base salary, performance incentives, phantom equity, benefits, RRSP match and a vehicle.
You will live in Alberta or Manitoba and travel regularly between the two regions.

Send your resume and a short note, one page at most, answering these three questions:
What is the largest profit and loss you have personally owned, and what happened to revenue and margin while you owned it?
Describe the hardest commercial negotiation you have led with a client. What was at stake, and how did it end?
What is the most challenging or complex change initiative you have led? What did the initiative achieve?

We read every note. Applications without one will not be considered.
